Diagnose Log Collection (diagnostic battery over SSH)

Tick one or more devices of the active ADOM, give the run a label, and SATOM runs that ADOM's read-only diagnostic battery (or your own get/show/diagnose commands) over SSH, saving each device's output as a labelled text file you can view or download.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsoperations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereAny device ADOM → Operations → Troubleshooting → Diagnose Log Collection (URL /web/logs/)

What is it?#

Diagnose Log Collection gathers diagnostic output from the devices of the active ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator) for a support case or a before/after comparison. For each selected device SATOM opens one SSH session, runs the ADOM's diagnostic battery, a list of read-only get / show / diagnose commands, and writes the output to a labelled .txt file.

An administrator chooses each ADOM's battery under Administrator → Diagnostic Battery. It is not a viewer of the appliance's attack or event logs (for those see Attack search).

What does it do?#

  • Runs the ADOM's battery, or your own commands, on many devices of that ADOM in one run. The page lists the battery read-only, with its source (Product default, or Chosen by an administrator on a date).
  • Checks every command before connecting: only get, show and diagnose (diag) are accepted, on every line and in every ;, &, | separated statement. A diagnose command whose name changes the device, never returns, floods the session or sends traffic is refused (see the battery rule).
  • Adapts the battery to each device's firmware build. A command that the build does not have, according to that build's discovery, is not sent. The report says SKIPPED: not present in <build>: ….
  • Tags an answer such as "Command fail" or "Parsing error" with [not available on this build].
  • Runs in the background and shows Progress (percentage, live log, and per device the number of commands ran, skipped and not available).
  • Keeps a history (Existing logs: File, When, Size) where each file can be viewed in the browser or downloaded.

Requirements#

  • Devices registered in the ADOM, with SSH reachable. SATOM logs in with the appliance's SSH user and SSH password when they are set, and otherwise with the API username and password (see Appliances). A FortiGate registered with a REST api-user and a FortiAuthenticator registered with an API key need these SSH fields.
  • Only one collection runs at a time (a run that started less than 15 minutes ago blocks a new one).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Every route requires the legacy config_write gate — for example operations.apply or appliances.apply (full list in Monitoring overview). It writes nothing to the device, but it opens an administrative SSH session with the stored credentials. Users without it get 403 and do not see the menu entry. Only devices of the current ADOM that are visible to you can be selected, and the history and file view show only logs of devices you can see. The link Edit in Administrator → Diagnostic Battery is shown only to holders of users.manage.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Existing logs lists and opens only files of devices visible to you; logs of other ADOMs' or hidden maintenance devices no longer appear.

How to use#

  1. Switch to the device ADOM (for example FortiGate) and open Operations → Troubleshooting → Diagnose Log Collection.
  2. Check the Diagnostic battery card: it lists the commands that will run.
  3. Under Devices () tick devices (Select all / None).
  4. Set Label (for example before, after, incident); default manual.
  5. Optionally open Custom commands (optional) and enter one command per line. Leave it empty to run the battery.
  6. Click Collect logs. Watch Progress.
  7. In Existing logs, click View to open a file, or download it.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Devices () Appliances of the active ADOM to collect from Yes fweb-01, fweb-02
Label Becomes part of the file name; non-alphanumeric characters become _ No before-upgrade
Custom commands One read-only command per line (get, show or diagnose); blank lines and # lines ignored. Held to the same battery rule. No get system status

Files are named <appliance id>_logs_<label>_<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.txt and stored in SATOM's data/diagnostics/ directory. Each file ends with the number of commands that ran and the number skipped.

The default batteries#

Until an administrator saves a battery for an ADOM, that ADOM runs its product default.

FortiWeb (28 commands, the same on FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6): get system status, get system performance, diagnose system update info, diagnose system mount list, diagnose system dbsync status, the diagnose system ha set (confd_status, dev-info, interface-macinfo, nodes, status, sync-stat), diagnose system securitylevel, diagnose hardware sysinfo vm, diagnose hardware cpu list, the diagnose hardware harddisk set (list, info, health, errors, attributes), diagnose hardware logdisk info, diagnose hardware interrupts list, diagnose hardware nic list, diagnose network info routing-table all, diagnose network route list, diagnose debug netstatlog show, diagnose network arp list, diagnose hardware mem list, diagnose debug memory. On a VM without HA, dbsync status, ha dev-info and debug netstatlog show print nothing; that is expected.

FortiADC: get system status, get system performance, diagnose hardware get sysinfo cpu, diagnose hardware get sysinfo memory, diagnose hardware get deviceinfo nic, diagnose system df, diagnose system memory, diagnose system ps, diagnose debug info. (diagnose hardware get sysinfo and deviceinfo on their own answer "Incorrect number of parameters" on 7.6.7 and 8.0.4.)

FortiGate: get system status, get system performance status, get hardware status, get system ha status, diagnose sys ha status, diagnose hardware deviceinfo disk, diagnose sys session stat, diagnose debug crashlog get, diagnose autoupdate versions, get router info routing-table all. (8.0.1 has no diagnose debug crashlog read.)

FortiAnalyzer: get system status, get system performance, diagnose system route list, diagnose system print loadavg, diagnose system print partitions, diagnose system ntp status, diagnose fortilogd lograte, diagnose debug sysinfo. (7.6.7 has no diagnose debug crashlog read.)

FortiAuthenticator: get system status, diagnose system ntp status, diagnose netlink interface list, diagnose netlink arp list, diagnose debug info.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-14: the page is called Diagnose Log Collection. The battery dropped diagnose hardware harddisk on its own (it only prints "you must specify cmd") and diagnose system ha export-eventlog (it needs parameters), and diagnose hardware cpu became diagnose hardware cpu list — measured on FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6, where the old forms returned no data.

ℹ️Note

Moved on 2026-10-14 (later the same day). The page now lives under Operations → Troubleshooting in all five device ADOMs; before, it was under Operations in the FortiWeb ADOM only. It runs the ADOM's battery, which an administrator can change under Diagnostic Battery. diagnose debug proxy log 3 left the FortiWeb battery, because it printed nothing on 7.6.8 or 8.0.6 and the device describes diagnose debug proxy as set/get (the number sets a debug level). SSH now logs in with the appliance's SSH user and SSH password. Before this change it always sent the API password, which FortiAuthenticator's SSH refuses.

Example#

🧪Example — Before/after a firmware upgrade

Before the window, collect from fweb-01 and fweb-02 with label before. After the upgrade, collect again with label after. Download both files of each device and compare them, or attach them to the support case. If the new build dropped a command, the after file shows it as SKIPPED: not present in <build> (once that build has been discovered) or tags its answer [not available on this build].

Result#

  • One .txt per device in the history.
  • An audit entry logs.collect with the ADOM, the device count, label, device names, the number of commands, how many were skipped per device, and whether they were custom.

Troubleshooting#

"Refused: '…': 'set' is not a read-only command — only diag, diagnose, get, show are allowed in the console"#

A custom line starts with a verb that is not a read. The whole run is refused; nothing is executed. Remove or fix the line.

"Refused: '…': '…' changes the device state"#

A custom diagnose line contains a word that changes the device, such as kill, clear, reset, delete, failover, sysrq or set. Abbreviations count: diag sys kil reads as kill. The whole run is refused. Remove the line.

"Refused: '…': '…' runs until interrupted, floods the session or sends traffic, so it cannot run in an unattended battery"#

A custom line such as diagnose sniffer packet, diag sys top, a ping or a traceroute never returns or sends traffic. Run it interactively on the device instead.

"Enter at least one get, show or diagnose command."#

The custom box contained only blank or comment lines. Clear it to use the battery, or add a command.

"This ADOM has no diagnostic battery."#

The ADOM's battery is empty. An administrator can reset it to the product default under Diagnostic Battery.

"Select at least one device."#

No device was ticked (or the ticked ones are not devices of this ADOM visible to you).

"… the SSH password cannot be read (…)"#

The separate SSH password of that appliance cannot be decrypted or fetched. Enter it again on the appliance's edit page.

"a collection is already running"#

Another run started less than 15 minutes ago is still in progress. Wait for it to finish.

A command shows "SKIPPED: not present in "#

The device's firmware build has no such command, according to the discovery of that build. This is expected on a mixed fleet. To change the battery, use Diagnostic Battery.

A command shows "SKIPPED (blocked): …"#

The battery rule refuses the command on this device. The usual cause is that the discovery of the device's build describes the command, or a parent, as changing something. Remove it from the battery.

A collected file is missing from Existing logs#

The device it came from is not visible to you (another ADOM, or a maintenance device your profile cannot see). Users who can see that device still find it.

A device fails in the progress list#

SSH could not connect or authenticate (or the host key changed). Check SSH access and the SSH user and password on the appliance; other devices in the run continue.

Advanced#

Advanced Behaviour details
  • Each device's plan (which commands run, which are skipped and why) is computed when you click Collect logs, from the device's firmware and the stored discovery catalogs. A build that has not been discovered yet runs every command that passes the rule.
  • Progress is stored in a file (_progress.json in the diagnostics directory) so every SATOM worker reports the same state.
  • The history lists only the collected files whose device (the appliance id at the start of the file name) is visible to you; opening another file's URL answers 404.
  • Opened from the Global ADOM by URL, the page falls back to the FortiWeb ADOM.
  • Host keys are trusted on first use and then pinned (see Security model).
